cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which acidic ternary acid is formed when Sulfur Trioxide gas ($$\text{SO}_3$$) reacts with water?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Write the chemical equation**
Reacting a nonmetallic oxide with water forms a ternary acid:
$$\text{SO}_3\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \longrightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)}$$

**Step 2: Identify the product name**
$$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$ is named **Sulfuric acid**.

**Step 3: Final Answer**
The correct option is **Sulfuric acid ($$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$)**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the characteristic color of the acid-base indicator phenolphthalein when added to a basic (alkaline) solution?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall indicator color transitions**
Phenolphthalein has a pH transition range of $$8.2 - 10.0$$.
*   In acidic solutions ($$\text{pH} < 7$$), it is **colorless**.
*   In basic solutions ($$\text{pH} > 7$$), it turns **bright pink**.

**Step 2: Final Answer**
The correct color in base is **Bright Pink**.

cards.q: According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, an acid is defined as a substance that does which of the following?

options.B: Accepts a proton ($$\text{H}^+$$) from another substance.
options.C: Donates a proton ($$\text{H}^+$$) to another substance.
options.D: Reacts with metals to form hydrogen gas.

cards.why:
**Step 1: State the Brønsted-Lowry acid-base definition**
According to Brønsted and Lowry, acid-base reactions involve proton transfer.
*   An acid is a **proton ($$\text{H}^+$$) donor**.
*   A base is a **proton acceptor**.

**Step 2: Conclusion**
Therefore, the correct statement is **Donates a proton ($$\text{H}^+$$) to another substance.**

cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify strong vs. weak acids**
Strong acids completely dissociate in water, while weak acids only partially dissociate.

**Step 2: Classify options**
*   $$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$ (acetic) is weak.
*   $$\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$$ (carbonic) is weak.
*   $$\text{HF}$$ (hydrofluoric) is weak.
*   $$\text{HCl}$$ (hydrochloric) is a strong mineral acid.

**Step 3: Final Answer**
The correct strong acid is **$$\text{HCl}$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following salts is classified as an acid salt because it retains a replaceable hydrogen atom?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Define normal and acid salts**
*   Normal salts have all acidic Hydrogen atoms replaced by metal cations.
*   Acid salts retain one or more replaceable Hydrogen atoms in their formulas.

**Step 2: Evaluate the options**
Only Sodium Bicarbonate ($$\text{NaHCO}_3$$) retains a Hydrogen ($$\text{H}$$) atom in its ionic structure.

**Step 3: Final Answer**
The acid salt is **$$\text{NaHCO}_3$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Calculate the pH of an aqueous solution where the hydrogen ion concentration is exactly $$[\text{H}^+] = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Apply the pH formula**
$$\text{pH} = -\log[\text{H}^+]$$

**Step 2: Substitute and solve**
$$\text{pH} = -\log(1.0 \times 10^{-3}) = -(-3) = 3.0$$

**Step 3: Final Answer**
The pH is **$$3.0$$**.

cards.title: Salts
body: Salt = acid H replaced by a metal/ammonium. Prepare: metal + acid, carbonate + acid, base + acid, precipitation for insolubles.

cards.title: Lab pattern for salts
body: Soluble salt from a metal, base or carbonate: add the solid to warm acid until some remains (acid is used up), filter off the extra solid, evaporate until crystals form, cool, filter, dry. Excess solid method avoids leftover acid in the crystals. Insoluble salt: mix two solutions that swap partners, filter, wash, dry — precipitation.

Titration hygiene: rinse pipette with the solution it will measure, burette with the other, conical flask with distilled water only (you will add a known volume next). Repeat to concordant titres. Indicator choice: strong acid / strong base — almost any; weak acid / strong base — phenolphthalein.
pH is a log scale. Jumping from 4 to 3 is not “a bit more acid” — it is ten times the [H⁺]. Universal indicator is a rainbow estimate; a pH meter is a number.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: According to solubility rules, which of the following sulfates is insoluble in water and will precipitate out of solution?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall sulfate solubility rules**
All sulfates are soluble *except* those of Barium ($$\text{Ba}^{2+}$$), Calcium ($$\text{Ca}^{2+}$$), and Lead ($$\text{Pb}^{2+}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the insoluble sulfate**
Therefore, Barium Sulfate ($$\text{BaSO}_4$$) is insoluble in water and forms a solid precipitate.

**Step 3: Final Answer**
The insoluble sulfate is **$$\text{BaSO}_4$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following represents a triprotic acid capable of donating three protons per molecule?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Define protic classifications**
*   Monoprotic: 1 acidic hydrogen ($$\text{HCl}$$, $$\text{HNO}_3$$).
*   Diprotic: 2 acidic hydrogens ($$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$).
*   Triprotic: 3 acidic hydrogens ($$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$).

**Step 2: Conclusion**
Therefore, the triprotic acid is **$$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$**.
